newsitem.title: USA: US spot resids again gain slightly on stable crude.
newsitem.headline: US spot resids again gain slightly on stable crude.

text.p: U.S. spot fuel oil prices mostly edged higher again Thursday in quiet trade, boosted by a relatively stable crude market and firmer physical gas quotes despite fairly mild East Coast weather, sources said.

"With this weather, we're not burning much of anything, but oil definitely beats gas," said one East Coast utility source, noting relatively light air conditioning loads this week and forecasts for more of the same next week despite an expected warmup this weekend.
In New York Harbor, physical one percent firmed slightly to the $16.50-75 a barrel level, with September one percent paper talked steady early in the 16.40-65 area.
NYH 0.3 percent high pour, still underpinned by a significant New York utility August buy program, held steady at $18.50-75.
High sulphurs in New York again scored modest gains, with 2.2 percent now quoted near $16, traders said.
At the U.S. Gulf, one percent was up slightly at about $16.50, while three percent gained a quarter or more to about the $16 level, traders said.
No NYH or USG deals were reported.

New York city gate gas prices rallied more than a dime Thursday to the low-to-mid $2.70s/mmBtu, or $17.33 a barrel equivalent. Gas at Henry Hub, the NYMEX delivery point, gained about 10 cents to the mid-$2.50s/mmBtu, or about $16.07 a barrel.
